intro.title: RBAC Permission Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook that checks user permissions based on Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). You will learn how to encapsulate permission logic into a reusable function using the core React concept of hooks. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript for type safety, and the `useState` and `useEffect` hooks to manage state and side effects. By the end, you'll have a hook that can determine if a user has a specific permission, which you can use to conditionally render UI elements in your application.
intro.usecase: RBAC permission hooks are essential in enterprise applications where different user roles need access to different features. In admin dashboards, hooks control which users can view analytics, manage users, or configure settings. E-commerce platforms use them to restrict inventory management to warehouse staff while allowing customer support to process refunds. Financial applications implement RBAC hooks to ensure only authorized personnel can approve transactions or access sensitive reports. This pattern prevents unauthorized access while maintaining clean, reusable permission logic across components.
